concerns: Manufacturability and scale-up: capture-based enrichment selected for mucin resistance may be difficult to scale (cost, resin/ligand availability, reuse, and lot-to-lot ligand performance). Yields of the capture-enriched fraction are unknown and may be insufficient to define a manufacturable drug-substance even if analytically distinct (supported by ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi dependency on source-cell scalability).

Process sensitivity: the capture step and simulated nasal-mucus/device passage introduce multiple process variables (mucin composition, shear profile, capture reagent conditioning) that can cause fragile assay-dependent pass/fail results; small changes may flip outcome, reducing robustness for release decisions (ev-misev2023-quality-framework recommends orthogonal characterization and control of process variables).

Measurement feasibility and interference: simulated mucus and device residues can interfere with immuno-capture and activity assays, producing false negatives/positives; rigorous spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility controls are necessary but add complexity and potential residual uncertainty (proposal acknowledges this dependency).

Lot comparability and biological variability: conditioned-medium lots from MSCs can vary; the qualitative pass/fail endpoint requires reproducible success across >=3 independent lots—this is challenging biologically and will pressure upstream cell-bank and process controls (ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi highlights source-cell consistency as a translational consideration).

Stability and relevance to in vivo exposure: preservation of a membrane-protected signal after simulated mucus/device passage in vitro may not predict survival, biodistribution, or detectability after intranasal dosing in larger species; macaque data showing poor intranasal detectability (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution) indicate species- and formulation-dependent delivery failures that are not addressed by the in vitro gate alone.

Scale-up risk: if the capture chemistry is treated as a product-defining gate, significant downstream CMC investment will be required to validate ligand supply, process robustness, cleaning/validation, and acceptable yields; failure at scale would force programmatic rework.

Quality-attribute relevance: as currently proposed the attribute is exploratory/qualitative and not a validated potency or release assay. Without quantitative, orthogonal, and reproducible readouts and defined acceptance criteria, it has limited immediate value for release or stability testing (consistent with ev-misev2023-quality-framework recommendations).

Potential confounders: capture reagents may enrich non-EV particles (lipoproteins or aggregates) that resist mucin and mimic membrane-protected signal; detergent/protease protection assays reduce but do not eliminate this risk—additional orthogonal identity assays will be required (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).
conclusion: Supported as an exploratory analytical/selection strategy but with substantial practical and translational risks that must be resolved before any CMC adoption. The proposal aligns with community recommendations for orthogonal intact-EV analytics (ev-misev2023-quality-framework), addresses source-cell and scale considerations noted in rodent-clonal vs primary comparisons (ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi), and is motivated by documented intranasal detectability limits in a primate model (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution). Key gaps remain in capture-reagent specificity, process yields, and large-species in vivo relevance; these drive high scale-up and lot-comparability risk and limit immediate QA applicability.
evidence_gap: No direct evidence provided that a mucin-resistant capture chemistry (1) selectively enriches bona fide membrane-enclosed small EVs rather than non-EV particles under mucus/device stresses, (2) yields manufacturing-relevant material quantities, or (3) predicts recoverable intranasal exposure in large species; experimental data on capture specificity, enrichment yield, and NHP bridging are missing.
